analyst_view.overall: RB Leipzig (30th) and Lens (33rd) both have 3 points from four games and need a win to stay in the race for the top 24. Leipzig are 4th in the Bundesliga under Martin Demichelis and won 5-1 at Union Berlin, but centre-back Castello Lukeba is out with a bruised knee and Ouedraogo and Guiu are still injured (all counted by the numbers); Demichelis expects Lens to press and attack because they 'desperately need the three points'. Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in Didier Digard's first game after the 9-1 loss at Como; Gradit, Ivanovic and Bulatovic are back in the squad, but right-back Ruben Aguilar (hamstring) and Michael Cuisance (ill) are out, Chavez is not registered and Edouard is still out (counted). A lineup reported by Lensois.com has Digard switching to a back three with Ganiou and Abdulhamid as wing-backs, Haidara and Titraoui in midfield and Sima up front, which is one report, not confirmed. Slovak referee Ivan Kruzliak, a little below average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, adding about 8% to Leipzig for their recent scoring and about 6% to Lens for Lukeba's absence. Lens are reported to switch to a back three, which could make them a bit harder to break down, but they have conceded 17 in their last six and Gradit is only just back, so the two points cancel. I stay at 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, split fairly evenly, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Last night I leaned slightly up for Digard's wide, crossing style, but the reported lineup puts a centre-back, Ganiou, at left wing-back and loses Aguilar on the right, so Lens look less of a crossing side tonight. Leipzig still attack wide through Nusa and Raum, so I drop the lean and stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Leipzig's quieter recent record (-8%) and Ivan Kruzliak's slightly low card rate (-5.4%) counted. Both sides need the win and Lens should press, as Demichelis expects, but there is no history of bad blood and nothing concrete to size, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots, adding about 7% to Leipzig for their busy recent shooting and trimming Lens (-9%) for their low count. Lens are without Cuisance and Edouard, two of their creators, while Sima and Ivanovic are back as attacking options, so the news points both ways and I stay at 28.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target and already add about 15% to Leipzig for how often they have tested goalkeepers lately. Leipzig plan to keep the ball and build from the back against a Lens defence missing Aguilar and still settling under a new coach, which is roughly what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 11.5.
